text.tspan: Film one swing down the line at the range. AIcoach
writes back the way a good coach would: what the
fault is, where it comes from, how sure it is, and
the one drill to take to your next bucket. When the
video cannot support an answer, it says so.
Down the line only · mp4 or mov, up to 15 seconds · 120 fps recommended
Three verified faults: early extension, loss of posture, over the top

svg.text: Hips 7% of body height toward the ball

text.tspan: ory, this was a clean clip, and the answer is clear.
At address your backside sits on the line we drew up
from it. By impact your hips have moved 7% of your
body height past that line, toward the ball¹. The rule table
calls early extension at 4%, so we are sure of this one.
“It may feel like you stay down, but at impact
your hips have moved toward the ball.”
From the range to the letter,
in three steps.
You will be standing at the range with a phone and a few
minutes between shots. Everything here is sized for that.
Prop your phone at hand height on your bag,
2.4–3.7 m behind you, looking down the target
line. 120 fps if your phone has it. One swing
per clip, whole body and club in frame.
Send the clip from your phone browser: mp4 or
mov, up to 15 seconds. Nothing is kept after
the analysis unless you tick Save to my swing
library.
Pose, swing events, measurements, the rule
table, then the explanation. You get one
fault chain, one drill and one mobility
exercise. Or an honest “Cannot analyse”.
It would
rather say less
than guess.
Most swing apps hand you a list of
deviations and leave you to work out
which one matters. AIcoach shows how
sure it is about every measurement,
explains each link of the cause, and
stops where the evidence stops.
Every number on a result carries
a confidence band. No exceptions.

svg.text: Measured relative to body height at address, so camera distance does not change the answer.

text.tspan: When the clip cannot support an answer, there
is no guessed fault. You get the reasons,
each linked to the filming guide step that
fixes it:
If your swing has none of the three verified
faults, it says so instead of forcing one on
you. Anything it notices outside the rule
table is labelled plainly:
Weight appears to move toward the trail
side at the top.
The rule table,
in three entries.
The MVP covers three faults, each decided by a fixed rule with
a configurable threshold. Each comes with its likely cause, one
drill and one mobility exercise.
Hips move toward the ball, address
to impact
Restricted hip rotation
Wall drill
90/90 hip rotation
Posture angle change in the
downswing vs address
Weak hip hinge or tight hamstrings
Alignment-stick head drill
Hip-hinge / hamstring mobility
Hand path in transition above the
backswing path
Upper body starts the downswing
Pump drill
Open books
Capped at medium confidence while measured from the hand
path.

svg.text: Anything outside the table is labelled “Unverified, confirm with a coach”, and never comes with a drill.

text.tspan: Then write back
to your coach.
Under every result you can ask about it in
plain words. The answers are drawn only from
that analysis: no new faults, no new numbers,
no drills it did not give you. If the analysis
cannot answer, the coach says so.
Why does it feel like I’m staying down when I’m not?
Your hips move forward rather than up, and forward is hard to feel. In
Plate II your hips sit 7% of your body height closer to the ball than at
address¹. The wall drill makes it something you can feel: if your trail
glute leaves the wall before impact, that is the movement the video
shows.

svg.text: ¹ Hips move toward the ball · 7% · confidence: high
Answers are based only on this analysis.
